title: A new apartment near Zurich
subtitle: A purchase read before the reservation is signed
note: An example of how a buyer reads a purchase. Varenta Immobilien AG, an invented name, stands in for a Swiss property developer checked in a real run; names and numbers are replaced, the findings are not. Nothing here says any company is party to any sale, and nothing is alleged. Every finding is an Antevo engine's answer on the date shown.

tries.label: The seller and the deposit, check by check
tries.source: Antevo Companies and Antevo Guard, 25 Nov 2026 · Zefix, SHAB, GLEIF, OFAC, EU, UK and SECO lists, domain registries and public DNS. One of Guard's four sources, the certificate logs, did not answer.

items.name: Who sells?
evidence: Varenta Immobilien AG, seat in canton Zurich: active in the Swiss commercial register
Its stated purpose: building and managing property, holdings, and buying and selling property

items.name: Is it on a sanctions list?
evidence: Not found under its name or identifiers on the OFAC, EU, UK and SECO lists, read 25 November 2026
Not being listed is not the same as unrestricted: ownership by a listed party needs its own check

items.name: What changed lately?
evidence: 15 register notices since March 2019; one this year, on 15 January 2026
The file gives the date and the notice, not what changed: the text is on shab.ch

items.name: Which company signs?
evidence: Seven register entries carry the name: Varenta Immobilien AG, Varenta Holding AG, Varenta Management AG, Varenta Zürich Nord AG, Varenta FM Service AG and two branches in Lausanne
GLEIF lists no parent for Varenta Immobilien AG; owners who are people are not public in Switzerland

items.name: Where does the deposit go?
evidence: Its domain has been registered since 30 November 1999 and points to a web server; nothing contradicts the record in the three sources that answered
It publishes no DMARC mail policy, so mail claiming to come from it is easier to fake; the certificate logs were not checked

steps.label: Before you sign, with the links

items.do: Read the seller's register extract: the exact company and who may sign for it
items.why: Seven entries carry the name; the reservation and the deed should name the same one.
The file gives the date; the notice says what changed.

items.do: Before paying the reservation deposit, confirm the payee and the account by phone, on a number you looked up yourself
items.why: A payment instruction by email is the weak point; ask where the deposit is held and on what terms it comes back.

items.do: Order the land register extract for the plot: the owner, easements, mortgage notes and pre-emption rights
items.why: The land register is kept by the canton; in the canton of Zurich the notary's offices keep it.

items.do: Read the public-law restrictions on the plot: zoning, building lines, contaminated sites
items.why: They bind the plot whoever owns it.

items.do: If you live abroad, check whether you need a permit to buy
items.why: Swiss law limits purchases by persons abroad; the canton decides.

items.do: Ask two lenders for dated offers, SARON-linked and fixed, and how long each offer holds
items.why: The bank tests what you can carry at about 5%, not at today's rate.

items.do: Have the draft deed read before the notary's appointment
items.why: In Switzerland a property sale is valid only as a notarised deed; a reservation is not the purchase.

sections.title: The market
sections.so_what: Scarcity holds the price up while the pace slows and asking prices are cut more often: the asking price is where the conversation starts, and what happens to the deposit if you step back is worth settling first.
evidence: Swiss condominium prices rose 3.9% on the year in the third quarter of 2026, and 0.8% on the quarter (transaction prices)
The estimate for 2026 is a rise of 2.5% for owner-occupied homes in the canton of Zurich, against 4.0% nationally
Vacancy was 0.9% nationally at the June 2026 count, the sixth yearly fall; in the city of Zurich 0.11%, 252 homes
Signs of saturation: asking prices are cut more often during marketing, and some buyers step back after paying a reservation deposit
sections.source: Antevo Research, real estate desk, 25 Nov 2026

sections.title: The mortgage
sections.so_what: What the bank will lend is set by its test at about 5%, not by today's rate; SARON or fixed is a choice about who carries a rise in 2027.
evidence: SARON-linked mortgages a little over 1%, ten-year fixed around 2% (early October 2026: a range, not a quote)
SNB policy rate 0.00% (October 2026), held since June 2025; Swiss inflation rose to 1.5% in October
Forecasters expect a first rise in 2027, most of them in March, and 0.5 to 0.75% by the end of 2027; some expect a move on 10 December

The rules lenders apply: at least 20% own funds, half of it not from the pension fund; costs at about 5% interest plus about 1% upkeep within a third of gross income; the loan paid down to two thirds within 15 years

sections.title: The price against history
sections.so_what: Swiss prices have fallen for a decade before. How long you expect to stay is part of the price: a short stay leaves your own funds exposed to the entry year.
evidence: Swiss real house prices stood at 140.9 on the OECD index at the end of June 2026, up 3.7% on the year
The last peak was 103.6 at the end of 1989; prices then fell 38% to early 2000 and passed the 1989 level again only at the end of 2017, 28 years later
Prices stand at 124.9% of their long-term average against incomes and 131.2% against rents (OECD, June 2026)
Credit is 11.8 points below its trend against the economy (BIS credit-to-GDP gap, March 2026): this rise was not built on loose lending
sections.source: Antevo Executive Brief, macro series since 1970, and Antevo Research, 25 Nov 2026

sections.title: Market strain
sections.so_what: Fixed-rate offers follow bond yields. With bond markets unsettled an offer can change within days: ask how long it holds.
evidence: Week of 20 November 2026: elevated, down from high (3.8 times) the week before
Bond links are breaking at 2.1 times their normal rate, all of them weakening; credit is calm at 0.5 times
Provisional: 697 of 753 pairs were read this week. It describes, it does not forecast
sections.source: Antevo Tremor Index, week of 20 Nov 2026

links.text: The seller is on the register and on none of the lists read, while its mail domain publishes no DMARC mail policy: the weak point is the payment instruction, not the company.
Prices still rise by 3 to 4% a year while the real index stands 36% above its 1989 peak: scarcity and stretch at once, so the holding period carries the risk.
Rates are low and expected to rise from 2027 while bond links break at twice their normal rate: a fixed offer may not hold for long.
Banks test at about 5% while prices sit a quarter above their long-term average against incomes: for many buyers the bank's test, not the asking price, sets the limit.

watch: Swiss inflation for November on 2 December, then the SNB's assessment on 10 December 2026
A first SNB rate rise, which most forecasters expect in March 2027
New register notices for the seller (Antevo Companies alerts at most once a day)
Asking-price cuts and time on the market in the area
1 January 2029: the imputed rental value is due to end, and with it the deductions for mortgage interest and upkeep
